issues.text: Right after 'The two measurements can disagree' the paragraph compares method-level cohesion with class-level cohesion before it gets to coupling. I had to re-read to see that 'the two measurements' means cohesion vs coupling, not method level vs class level.
issues.quote: The two measurements can disagree. Each method in `PlaceOrderSplit` does one focused job: high cohesion at the method level.
issues.fix: Open the paragraph with 'Cohesion and coupling can disagree.' instead of 'The two measurements can disagree.'

issues.text: 'pricing now depends on another class' says the split created this dependency, but the situation only says the teammate split the method into four private methods. I could not tell when or why the discount moved out into `NamingAfter`; I just accepted it.
issues.quote: and pricing now depends on another class, `NamingAfter`
issues.fix: In the situation, after 'a short `Place` that calls four private methods, one per job', add: 'and the pricing method gets its discounted total from another class, `NamingAfter`.'

issues.text: 'two items at 1,100,000 VND' can be read as 1,100,000 for both together. Only with 1,100,000 each (2,200,000 total) do I get 2,010,000 and 2,090,000, so I had to try both readings to check the expected result.
issues.quote: for a loyal customer ordering two items at 1,100,000 VND
issues.fix: Replace with 'for a loyal customer ordering quantity 2 at 1,100,000 VND each'.

issues.text: Option c is now clearly the longest option and the only one with a two-part reason, so it can be picked by length.
issues.quote: False, because one asks whether a unit's own parts belong together, the other whether changing it drags other units along.
issues.fix: Shorten c (e.g. 'False, because one looks inside a unit, the other at what it depends on.') or give b and d a similar two-part reason.

issues.text: The comment also claims 'no cohesion problem left', and section 4 says the class still has low cohesion because it holds four jobs. Option a and its explanation only answer the coupling half, so I wondered whether an option about class-level cohesion was missing.
issues.quote: The split improved cohesion only; `PlaceOrderSplit` still relies on the result of `NamingAfter.TotalVnd`.
issues.fix: Add one clause to the correct explanation: 'and the class still holds all four jobs, so its cohesion problem is not gone either.'
